reviewedFrom: B11.1 and B11.2 definitions of done (advisor-plans/013) and docs/books-revenue-recognition.md §2/§4b/§4c/§4d.

explicit-policy-by-kind.derivation: Fixed-price, time-and-materials and all three cost-plus jobs earn over time (cost-to-cost), so their billing is deferred in 2350 until earned; a home sold under a purchase agreement earns at closing, so its invoice is revenue when invoiced; a standalone service invoice (no project) is revenue when invoiced. Each job's policy is recorded when it first posts, inferred from its billing settings and labeled as not reviewed.

settings-change-cannot-rewrite.derivation: A fixed-price job posts a July invoice as deferred billing and its policy is recorded. Its contract is then re-typed as a purchase agreement. Re-projecting posts nothing new for July, and an August invoice is still deferred: the recorded policy governs. The register flags that the settings now say 'at closing'.

approved-change-from-its-date.derivation: July closes with the job earning over time. A change to 'at closing' dated July 20 is refused because July is closed under the current method. The same change dated August 1 is proposed by the owner, cannot be approved by the owner, and is approved by the accountant. The July invoice stays deferred; an August invoice earns when invoiced and names the policy. The approved policy cannot be edited. The register shows the approved policy from Aug 1 with the inferred baseline before it.

expected.intoClosedMonth: July 2026 is closed under the current method. Date the change after 2026-07-31, or reopen July 2026 first.
expected.selfApproval: A revenue policy is approved by someone other than the person who proposed it

superseded-contracts-reconstructible.derivation: A sale posts in July and its policy (at closing) is recorded; its agreement is later superseded by one effective in October. Re-projection posts nothing new: the recorded policy still decides July. A legacy sale whose only July-era agreement was already superseded, with no recorded policy, cannot be decided: its invoice is a finding naming the missing historical policy. Once a policy from the start is proposed and approved, it posts, earned when invoiced.

mixed-contracts-reviewed.derivation: A job with a construction contract (earns over time) and a lot-sale purchase agreement (earns at closing) in force together is refused until each contract has an approved policy; its invoices are findings with that cure. After approval, the construction invoice is deferred, the lot-sale invoice is earned when invoiced, and only the construction contract has a WIP position.

cost-plus-earns-once.derivation: A cost-plus-10% job incurs a $100,000.00 vendor bill and a $5,000.00 manual billable adjustment in September; billed from costs that is 100,000 + 10,000 + 5,000 + 500 = $115,500.00, posted as deferred billing (2350). The job is complete: WIP is prepared with the expected total billable ($115,500.00) as the transaction price and the $100,000.00 job cost as the estimate, so it is 100% complete and earns $115,500.00. Revenue equals what was billed, earned once; 2350 nets to zero; job cost $100,000.00.

billed-cost-corrections.derivation: Bills A ($10,000) and B ($5,000) are billed at cost + 10%: $16,500.00. A is returned to pending (credited once: -$11,000), re-approved unchanged (billable again), returned to pending again (the unbilled rebill is voided; no second credit), and re-approved re-coded into two lines totalling $10,000 ($11,000 billable). B is returned to pending and its credit (-$5,500) is absorbed with a reason. A new bill C ($2,000) arrives. The next invoice carries A's credit, A's re-coded cost and C: -11,000 + 11,000 + 2,200 = $2,200.00; B's absorbed credit is not billed. Billed rows cannot be edited or deleted. Voiding the first invoice is refused because A's credit is already on the second.

expected.voidFirstInvoice: Failed to void invoice: This cost's credit is already on another invoice; void or credit that invoice first

gmp-cap-and-settlement.derivation: A $50,000.00 GMP (cost plus fee, not to exceed) bills $40,000 at cost + 10% = $44,000.00. A further $11,000 would reach $55,000: refused, then billed with an override recorded as an event. An approved change order raises the GMP by $10,000 to $60,000, so a further $3,300 ($58,300 billed) bills without an override. A second $50,000 GMP job bills $33,000 and then has a $2,200 cost still unbilled when it completes: settlement is refused until it is billed. Billed within the GMP is then $35,200, so savings are $14,800.00, split 50/50: the builder's $7,400.00 is billed once (one invoice even though two requests race); the owner's $7,400.00 was never billed and needs no invoice.

expected.settleWithUnbilledCost: Bill the 1 remaining cost inside the GMP before settling savings.
